It is one of the things that so many fans love about classics like Law & Order . They are digestible single-episode cases, and you can drop in at practically any point. That also means that there is rarely any development for the characters. However, Kathy Bates \' 2024 reboot of Matlock broke the traditional legal procedural formula, and does a brilliant job of balancing the case of the week with the larger storyline. What Is Kathy Bates\' CBS Series \'Matlock\' About? Matlock stars Jason Ritter, Kathy Bates, and Skye P. Marshall Image via: CBS Matlock is a gender-swapped reboot of Andy Griffith’s classic Matlock , which ran from 1986 to 1995. In the updated version, the series takes place in a world where the original series was also a fan-favorite legal drama and a favorite of protagonist Madeline Matlock’s daughter. Kathy Bates plays the titular role as a retired lawyer who moves her husband and grandson with her to New York, comes out of retirement, and joins the law firm that she suspects is responsible for the death of her daughter. Related CBS’ 95% RT Legal Drama Surges on Streaming as Viewers Flock for Season 2 Kathy Bates and Skye P. Marshall star in the twisty lawyer drama. Posts By Rahul Malhotra Oct 15, 2025 Besides Bates, the splendid cast also features Skye P. Marshal l as her co-lead, alongside others like Jason Ritter , Sam Anderson , and Leah Lewis . At the firm, Jacobson Moore, Bates, and Olympia (Marshall) work alongside first-year associates Sarah and Billy ( David Del Rio ). Jacobson Moore worked with WellBrexa, a pharmaceutical company, and Matty believes someone at the law firm hid documents that could\'ve prevented the opioid epidemic , which ultimately led to her daughter’s addiction and eventual overdose. \'Matlock\' Stands Out From Other Traditional Legal Procedurals in an Inventive Way If you look at Law & Order: Special Victims Unit , led by the fabulous Mariska Hargitay , each episode is a self-contained case. Largely, the cases don’t span multiple episodes, and the focus isn’t on overarching character arcs. This case-of-the-week legal procedural provides comfort food for fans who can drop in and watch any episode. Unfortunately, it also leads to characters tending to be static and not developing too much throughout the season. The focus is rarely on the regulars, which leads to storylines about their character growth moving at a snail\'s pace — or sometimes being nonexistent all together. For fans of serialized dramas, Matlock is a breath of fresh air. It’s one of the rare legal procedurals that seamlessly blends a case of the week with its overarching storyline led by Matlock and her search for truth . The case-of-the-week series tend to have limited coverage of a character, such as a romance or a personal story. Matlock allows for its characters to have multiple stories alongside the crime that week. For example, besides solving the case, Matlock is constantly balancing the true feelings and connections she is forming with Olympia, Sarah, and Billy with the reality that she\'s showing them a fake version of herself. This all comes to a tense moment when her husband expresses his worries about her stress levels, and an ambulance is even called. Instead of saving for one big reveal at the end of the season, Matlock follows in the footsteps of streaming shows, with cliffhangers and revelations occurring at the end of almost every episode. Better yet, the Matlock writers didn’t confine the storyline to just one season. In a recent Season 2 episode, Olympia revealed to Madeline that Julian suspects she is involved in the Welbrexa situation. The stakes seem higher, it doesn’t feel forced, and in Season 2, we get to see two influential lawyers pulling the strings and conspiring to uncover the truth . As more audiences expect serialized dramas and throughlines, this kind of story is perfect for the streaming era. Matty and Olympia\'s Dynamic Is Even More Complicated in \'Matlock\' Season 2 via CBS From the “sweet elderly lawyer” Matlock to the angry and hurt Madeline, to the complex grandma of Alfie, we get to see Bates\' brilliant character from all sides. In Season 2 , we also get to explore so many new stories. Olympia is now part of the Wellbrexa exposure plan , which creates an entirely new dynamic and plenty of opportunities for tension between the two leads. One moment in Season 2 that stands out is when Olympia and Matty have to show each other their phones because they don\'t trust one another. At the same time, Olympia covers for Matty with their colleagues and gives fake excuses for Matty\'s whereabouts. We get to see Olympia behave in a completely new way with Matty. She records an audio clip of Matty threatening her as leverage , which completely usurps the trust and friendship they built in the first season. Thanks to that relationship and that foundation, there is a part of Matty that wants to stay and help Olympia, and doesn’t want her family to get hurt as a result of their investigation. Bates has this kind of internal struggle masterfully on display. In addition, Olympia has to balance Matty while protecting the father of her children. Leaving this storyline in the first season would have been a huge missed opportunity. In a genre known for playing it safe, Matlock took a risk, and it\'s paying off in every possible way. And Watch This Great Movie Before It Leaves HBO Max in November 2025 By Blair Marnell October 30, 2025 TOP STORIES Click to share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Click to share on X (Opens in new window) X Richard Farnsworth, Frances Sternhagen in Misery Columbia Pictures/courtesy Everett Collection Tap Here To Add Us Weekly As A Trusted Source Add as a preferred source on Google Hollywood has been making Stephen King movies for almost five decades, but there are only a handful that could be described as “Oscar-winning films.” Misery , a psychological horror thriller from director Rob Reiner and screenwriter William Goldman , is one of those films, thanks to Kathy Bates . In a story without a whiff of the supernatural, Bates’ Annie Wilkes is one of the scariest characters King has ever created. Watch With Us has selected Misery as the one great movie you need to watch before it leaves HBO Max in November. And it’s a film you won’t forget. Related: Like \'The Long Walk\'? Then Watch These 3 Underrated Stephen King Movies Now It’s possible you saw the trailer for The Long Walk and were surprised to discover it was based on a novel written by Stephen King. It does seem that as long as the world keeps spinning, there will always be another King short story or novel you’ve never heard of that’s somehow being turned into […] Kathy Bates Gives a Chilling Performance From the outside, it sure looks like one of the things that scares King is his most overzealous fans. Annie Wilkes is emblematic of the best kind of fan interactions and the worst. One minute, she’s the biggest admirer of writer Paul Sheldon ( James Caan ) and the next she flies into a murderous rage because she learns that his latest novel has killed off her favorite character, Misery Chastain. Considering Paul is essentially her hostage in a remotely located home, that places him completely at her mercy. Bates’ performance is a masterclass of subtle expressions and actions when she isn’t angry. Just watch the looks on her face when she’s on-camera. The audience can sense the inner monologue of Annie’s mind without Bates having to say a word. Annie is capable of performing shocking acts of violence, and she only gets more frightening when she goes through with her threats. James Caan Is a Surprisingly Relatable Main Character Misery is a very humbling story for Paul, as Caan plays him like an arrogant star right up until the accident that almost kills him. Annie saves Paul’s life by bringing him to her cabin, and then subjects him to a living Hell. This is where the movie begins to unleash its horror. A barely mobile Paul has to find any advantage he can take over Annie, who towers over him. In the literary world, he’s a giant. Next to Annie, Paul seems quite small. It seemed like Matty ( Kathy Bates ) and Olympia ( Skye P. Marshall ) were on the path to rebuilding their friendship a couple of episodes ago on Matlock . They’re back to a stalemate as Julian ( Jason Ritter ) continues investigating Matty. He thinks she’s Belvin’s ( Patricia Belcher ) secret partner in crime. His gut tells him that something fishy is going on there, and it’s up to Olympia to convince him that he’s wrong. You can guess that’s a bit triggering as Matty gaslighting Olympia is still very fresh in her mind. Matty doesn’t seem to have any room in her heart to forgive Julian. That causes another impasse for her and Olympia, and it feels like we’re right back where we were at the start of the season with these two. Even a heartbreaking case that forces Matty to do some self-reflection doesn’t lead to her giving Julian any grace, and it makes it hard to see how the investigation continues from here. A Re-sentencing Case Pushes Matty To Take a Look in the Mirror Kathy Bates as Matty and Leah Lewis as Sarah on Matlock via CBS Olympia, Julian, and YouThree pick up a resentencing case who is serving a life sentence for pushing his abusive foster father down the stairs when he was a juvenile. Daniel Pearson ( Keyon Bowman ) has memory issues from the evening of the murder and the team is racing against the clock to gather the evidence to prove he has no history of violence and the incident with his foster father was an isolated incident. It requires tracking down Daniel’s whereabouts throughout the day of the murder, including a strip club which reminds Matty of her troubled childhood tagging along with her alcoholic mother to the bars to pick up men. Over the course of working on Daniel’s case, Olympia points out that she and Matty are not actually friends again. Olympia delivers one of the most poignant lines of the season, “I lied, but you’re a liar.” And she’s not wrong. Matty believes her lies are justified, but the truth is that she’s told a lot more of them than Olympia has and so it’s easy to see why Olympia is having trouble trusting her former office bestie. The accusation sends Matty into a tailspin and makes her think about her actions. Luckily, Sarah ( Leah Lewis ) and Billy ( David Del Rio ) are still focused on Daniel. They discover he was in the hospital at the time of his foster father’s death, which means he’s been serving time for a crime he didn’t commit. They don’t just get his sentence reduced, but they get his case thrown out and Daniel gets his entire life back. It’s a big victory for the team, and a good morale boost for Olympia, but things are still very sticky between her and Matty. The Julian Problem Has an Easy Solution Jason Ritter, Kathy Bates and Skye P. Marshall in 'Matlock' Image via CBS Matty is able to admit by the end of the episode that Olympia is correct about the amount she’s been lying. She’s been lying since she was a kid to protect herself, but she’s committed to staying honest with Olympia if they can be friends again. Olympia just isn’t ready to take that leap, and it’s because she feels so badly about what they’ve been doing to Julian . Julian tries to catch Matty out for helping Belvin twice over the course of the episode. He directly confronts her after she sneaks out of a hearing meeting with Daniel to get some tech advice from Edwin ( Sam Anderson ) and Alfie ( Aaron Harris ). Thanks to Olympia’s heads up that Julian is suspicious, Matty has an excuse for sneaking out of Belvin’s office, and a text message to corroborate the story. Julian still thinks there’s something wrong though so he concocts a plan to check Belvin’s old laptop to see if Matty really sent the text. Olympia plays the middle and gives Matty the heads up, so Matty and Alfie are able to get ahead of Julian’s side investigation. She even thinks of erasing herself from the firm’s new security cameras. That’s three strikes for Julian and he doesn’t take it well. His gut tells him that Matty is part of the Wellbrexa mess, and he’s right , but Matty doesn’t want him involved. So she makes Olympia complicit in gaslighting him and thinking that he’s a terrible person for suspecting a grandmother just trying to raise her grandson. Olympia and Julian may not be married anymore but it’s hard to watch her have to convince him that he’s losing it, and it makes sense that she’s reluctant to let Matty back into her life when this is the cost. It’s frustrating to watch Matty do all this self-reflection and not actually get to some place helpful . Yes, she comes clean to Olympia about why she lies, but she’s being bullish when it comes to Julian. He screwed up, badly. Matty is not innocent of crossing moral boundaries, though. She’s done a lot of questionable stuff in the name of finding out who hid the Wellbrexa documents. She thinks she’s judging Julian from a high horse, but it’s actually a glass house. The tension between Olympia and Matty could melt again if Matty would consider letting Julian into their plan. It would take Olympia out of the middle between Matty and the father of her children. Again, part of Matty’s request for the investigation to continue is for Julian to apologize, so he’s going to find out she’s involved at some point. Together, she and Olympia can convince him to help them bring down Senior ( Beau Bridges ). Icing Julian out like this is hurting everyone involved, including Matty, even if she doesn’t want to admit it. It’s getting harder and harder to watch Matty and Olympia only make shallow progress in repairing their friendship. Julian is the key to moving forward, and hopefully they realize that sooner rather than later. Matlock continues Thursdays at 9 PM ET on CBS. Apparently, I am not the only one impatient for Matty ( Kathy Bates ) and Olympia ( Skye P. Marshall ) to make up already on Matlock. Matty is also pushing for the pair to make up sooner rather than later , but Olympia is still taking time to process everything that has happened between the two of them. However, the job still requires them to work closely with each other, and the cracks in Olympia’s emotional walls are getting bigger and bigger with each and every case. There’s still hope, and we’ll have to cling to it for as long as we can. Matty and Olympia aren’t the only ones trying to forge new bonds in the office. Senior ( Beau Bridges ) sends Sarah ( Leah Lewis ) on a mission to get pictures of Julian’s ( Jason Ritter ) date book because Senior believes Julian is going to “poach clients” when he leaves. It’s more likely that Senior is suspicious of Eva’s ( Justina Machado ) constant presence in the New York office, but the snooping mission leads Sarah to genuinely bond with Julian. They both are kooky weirdos, and Julian grows to really appreciate Sarah, once he gets over the clinginess. Is he going to be able to deal when he finds out she was on his case on a mission for his father, though? Someone stop kicking this man while he’s down! Senior may be just starting to dig into Eva’s presence in the office, but we already know what’s going down. Matty and Olympia are helping her with a coup , which means some high-stakes action is coming to the Jacobson Moore office very soon. The Cruel Face of Addiction Appears in 'Matlock' Season 2, Episode 6 Marlene Forte as Sister Louise and Kathy Bates as Matty on Matlock via CBS Eva’s surface-level plans for her return trip to New York involve helping some nun friends with a zoning board hearing so they can continue running a homeless shelter out of their convent. She hands the case over to Olympia and team, who promptly handle the zoning board, only to find the nuns in the crosshairs of a civil suit when a rogue 9-1-1 call leads to drugs being found on the church premises. They’ve been allowing addicts to do “reduction of harm” shoot ups to help them survive the night, but that causes a visceral backlash against the convent when a video of a woman overdosing outside the church is shown in court. It’s a lot for the judge and the jury to see, and it’s also a lot for Matty to handle. Finding out that the nuns are giving addicts drugs hits a very sensitive nerve for Matty, who is immediately reminded of her daughter Ellie. It is always sad having to watch Matty confront the grief of losing her daughter, but this struggle isn’t just to give Kathy Bates more material for her Emmy reel. Working with the nuns helps Matty reacquaint herself with the human side of addiction — addicts are people that are trying. It makes her more lenient when it comes to Olympia not jumping to forgive her and it also makes her more understanding that Alfie’s father Joey can’t be “perfect in his sobriety.” The empathy we were hoping to see in Matty returns . Giving Joey some lenience when it comes to writing Alfie every day helps Alfie relax that his birth father doesn’t have to be a saint for him to have hope of having a relationship with him. Matty’s ability to find forgiveness in the face of such a triggering case also helps Olympia find her way a little closer to reconciling their friendship. She also expects Matty to be perfect, but that isn’t realistic. There’s going to be some back and forth and they have to figure out some way to be okay with that. In the end, the nuns lose the ability to provide controlled doses of narcotics to addicts, but retain the right to run a homeless shelter. They’re going to continue fighting the good fight, while Matty and Olympia turn their attention to their own massive battle. Sarah’s Side Mission Could Destroy Everything Leah Lewis as Sarah on Matlock via CBS Sarah is as shocked as anyone to find Senior approaching her while she prepares for the nun trial. New to the franchise is Wicked: For Good star Ariana Grande , who previously teamed up with Murphy on the horror-comedy series Scream Queens . And, as the announcement teases with a lengthy pause, Jessica Lange is making her return to the series, after last being seen briefly in 2018\'s Apocalypse season. The two-time Oscar winner previously starred in five seasons of the show, beginning with the inaugural Murder House . Despite her status as a perennial fan favorite, Lange had previously intimated in the past that she had no plans to return to the AHS televerse. In fact, on a red carpet earlier this year, when asked by an Irish radio station if she would be in the 13th season, Lange said, "Oh Christ, no. I mean, I haven\'t done it for more than 10 years, 12 years, so, no, I\'m not doing it." When the reporter followed up to ask if she would do the new season if approached, she said simply, "No," before walking away. A Somber Trip Down Memory Lane in 'Matlock' Season 2, Episode 4 Christine Kellogg-Darrin as “Gloria Russo”, Leah Lewis as “Sarah Franklin” and Kathy Bates as “Madeline Matlock” in Matlock Season 2, Episode 4 Image via CBS Olympia and crew take on a wrongful death suit in the case of the week to help an elderly widow get the money she needs to survive after her husband dies while trapped in his factory during a hurricane. The key part of their case is playing the widow’s final voicemail from her husband, which will drive home the emotional devastation of the loss to the jury. It takes tricking their opposing counsel into making the audio admissible, but it is the ticket Olympia needs to get a reasonable settlement on the table for their client. Matty is already in her feelings during the case as she buddies up with Deborah Palmer ( Surprise, it’s Melanie Lynskey making her acting debut with Kathy Bates, dreams come true! ). Deborah is Senior’s paramour that he took to Australia during the Wellbrexa case, and now is a freelance makeup artist. Matty goes in for a makeover that is comically awful (think Tammy Faye-level bad) but they bond over karaoke because that’s what Deborah and Senior did together in Australia (thanks uncovered expense reports!). It’s also Ellie’s favorite pastime, and getting closer to Deborah has Matty remembering her daughter’s karaoke baby shower. Ellie was sober for the event, but only newly so. Past Matty couldn’t just trust her daughter and allow herself to have a good time. She went above and beyond to ensure that Ellie was staying sober for her kid, but her constant checking and need for assurances created a wider gulf between her and her daughter, and nearly ruined a perfectly good day. Ellie would actually relapse a few weeks later, but singing on stage with Deborah and listening to their client talk about not wasting time with her husband has Matty feeling very wistful throughout the episode. There are multiple moments in this episode where we see glimpses of their friendship, and they’re the best parts of the entire episode. Optimists hold in there. When she evades Matty’s requests for a second karaoke date, Matty and Olympia surmise Senior had her sign an NDA. That means there’s a paper trail of damaging things being said in Australia, and they just have to find it . Luckily, they have a guy on the inside. Unluckily, that guy is also now suspicious of Matty’s involvement in the Wellbrexa investigation. Julian Is on the Trail, Is Time To Bring Him In? Senior’s latest attempt to humiliate Julian is to put him on the compliance committee, which means going around to every Jacobson Moore employee with the IT guy and briefing them on the new firm security measures after the leak. Olympia points out that this is a great opportunity for Julian to potentially get Senior’s login passwords so they can do the snooping they need to do to clear Julian of his wrongdoing in the Wellbrexa case. Julian comes up with a better idea when he spots Belvin’s ( Patricia Belcher ) login key and laptop by Senior’s assistant’s desk. He has his new IT buddy walk him through wiping the laptop clean and learns that Matty texted Belvin right before her meeting with the head of security. Senior’s old expense reports were also printed from Belvin’s account four minutes before that meeting, and Julian suspects that Matty is the one that printed them. She’s the one working with Belvin and therefore the real leaker . This seems like bad news on the surface. It gives Julian a lot of leverage in the whole investigation. It is a lot easier for him to hand Matty over to Senior and have him eviscerate her rather than continuing to risk his own neck to get the dirt on his dad. Matty absolutely won’t want him as part of the investigation. She’s having a hard enough time trusting Olympia. How could she possibly trust Julian when he hid the documents in the first place? However, as viewer, this is great. Jason Ritter is too good to have him play clueless for too long . Plus, one of Matty’s conditions for continuing to work with Olympia is that Julian has to apologize to her, Edwin ( Sam Anderson ), and Alfie ( Aaron Harris ). Obviously, Olympia and Matty are going to try and throw him off the scent first, but having Julian in the know is a really exciting possibility as we head further into the sophomore season . The more people that know about the investigation, the higher the stakes. It’s so juicy! Will they figure out a way to rope him in, or is he doomed to be the investigation lap dog forever? Published 4 weeks ago on October 31, 2025 By John Squires Pictured: Jessica Lange in 'American Horror Story: Freakshow' Ryan Murphy’s “American Horror Story” is coming back to life for Season 13, and the main cast featuring several returning favorites has been officially announced for Halloween. It sounds like the next season will be the ultimate “AHS” reunion special! Variety reports that Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe and Leslie Grossman will all be back for “American Horror Story: Season 13,” with newcomer Ariana Grande also signing on. Check out Ryan Murphy’s announcement teaser below and expect more soon. News of Jessica Lange’s involvement in Season 13 is particularly notable, as Lange hasn’t been part of the series for quite some time. In fact, she had recently outright stated that she won’t be involved in Season 13, but it seems she was playing coy at the time. Jessica Lange was of course a staple of the first four seasons of FX’s hit horror anthology between 2011 and 2015, her performances earning her two Primetime Emmy awards. She guest starred in 2018’s eighth season, reprising her original role as Constance Langdon. No word yet on the theme or title for “AHS” 13, which will arrive Halloween 2026 . Johnson/AP) NEW YORK — Sally Kirkland, a one-time model who became a regular on stage, film and TV, best known for sharing the screen with Paul Newman and Robert Redford in “The Sting” and her Oscar-nominated title role in the 1987 movie “Anna,” has died. She was 84. Her representative, Michael Greene, said Kirkland died Tuesday morning at a Palm Springs hospice. Friends established a GoFundMe account this fall for her medical care. They said she had fractured four bones in her neck, right wrist and left hip. While recovering, she also developed infections, requiring hospitalization and rehab. Kirkland acted in such films as “The Way We Were” with Barbra Streisand, “Revenge” with Kevin Costner, “Cold Feet” with Keith Carradine and Tom Waits, Ron Howard’s “EDtv,” Oliver Stone’s “JFK,” “Heatwave” with Cicely Tyson, “High Stakes” with Kathy Bates, “Bruce Almighty” with Jim Carrey and the 1991 TV movie “The Haunted,” about a family dealing with paranormal activity. She had a cameo in Mel Brooks’ “Blazing Saddles.” Her biggest role was in 1987’s “Anna” as a fading Czech movie star remaking her life in the United States and mentoring to a younger actor, Paulina Porizkova. Kirkland won a Golden Globe and earned an Oscar nomination along with Cher in “Moonstruck,” Glenn Close in “Fatal Attraction, Holly Hunter in ”Broadcast News" and Meryl Streep in “Ironweed.” Copyright 2025 The Associated Press. It is one of the things that so many fans love about classics like Law & Order . They are digestible single-episode cases, and you can drop in at practically any point. That also means that there is rarely any development for the characters. However, Kathy Bates \' 2024 reboot of Matlock broke the traditional legal procedural formula, and does a brilliant job of balancing the case of the week with the larger storyline. What Is Kathy Bates\' CBS Series \'Matlock\' About? Matlock stars Jason Ritter, Kathy Bates, and Skye P. Marshall Image via: CBS Matlock is a gender-swapped reboot of Andy Griffith’s classic Matlock , which ran from 1986 to 1995. In the updated version, the series takes place in a world where the original series was also a fan-favorite legal drama and a favorite of protagonist Madeline Matlock’s daughter. Kathy Bates plays the titular role as a retired lawyer who moves her husband and grandson with her to New York, comes out of retirement, and joins the law firm that she suspects is responsible for the death of her daughter. Related CBS’ 95% RT Legal Drama Surges on Streaming as Viewers Flock for Season 2 Kathy Bates and Skye P. Marshall star in the twisty lawyer drama. Posts By Rahul Malhotra Oct 15, 2025 Besides Bates, the splendid cast also features Skye P. Marshal l as her co-lead, alongside others like Jason Ritter , Sam Anderson , and Leah Lewis . At the firm, Jacobson Moore, Bates, and Olympia (Marshall) work alongside first-year associates Sarah and Billy ( David Del Rio ). Jacobson Moore worked with WellBrexa, a pharmaceutical company, and Matty believes someone at the law firm hid documents that could\'ve prevented the opioid epidemic , which ultimately led to her daughter’s addiction and eventual overdose. \'Matlock\' Stands Out From Other Traditional Legal Procedurals in an Inventive Way If you look at Law & Order: Special Victims Unit , led by the fabulous Mariska Hargitay , each episode is a self-contained case. Largely, the cases don’t span multiple episodes, and the focus isn’t on overarching character arcs. This case-of-the-week legal procedural provides comfort food for fans who can drop in and watch any episode. Unfortunately, it also leads to characters tending to be static and not developing too much throughout the season. The focus is rarely on the regulars, which leads to storylines about their character growth moving at a snail\'s pace — or sometimes being nonexistent all together. For fans of serialized dramas, Matlock is a breath of fresh air. It’s one of the rare legal procedurals that seamlessly blends a case of the week with its overarching storyline led by Matlock and her search for truth . The case-of-the-week series tend to have limited coverage of a character, such as a romance or a personal story. Matlock allows for its characters to have multiple stories alongside the crime that week. For example, besides solving the case, Matlock is constantly balancing the true feelings and connections she is forming with Olympia, Sarah, and Billy with the reality that she\'s showing them a fake version of herself. This all comes to a tense moment when her husband expresses his worries about her stress levels, and an ambulance is even called. Instead of saving for one big reveal at the end of the season, Matlock follows in the footsteps of streaming shows, with cliffhangers and revelations occurring at the end of almost every episode. Better yet, the Matlock writers didn’t confine the storyline to just one season. In a recent Season 2 episode, Olympia revealed to Madeline that Julian suspects she is involved in the Welbrexa situation. The stakes seem higher, it doesn’t feel forced, and in Season 2, we get to see two influential lawyers pulling the strings and conspiring to uncover the truth . As more audiences expect serialized dramas and throughlines, this kind of story is perfect for the streaming era. Matty and Olympia\'s Dynamic Is Even More Complicated in \'Matlock\' Season 2 via CBS From the “sweet elderly lawyer” Matlock to the angry and hurt Madeline, to the complex grandma of Alfie, we get to see Bates\' brilliant character from all sides. In Season 2 , we also get to explore so many new stories. Olympia is now part of the Wellbrexa exposure plan , which creates an entirely new dynamic and plenty of opportunities for tension between the two leads. One moment in Season 2 that stands out is when Olympia and Matty have to show each other their phones because they don\'t trust one another. At the same time, Olympia covers for Matty with their colleagues and gives fake excuses for Matty\'s whereabouts. We get to see Olympia behave in a completely new way with Matty. She records an audio clip of Matty threatening her as leverage , which completely usurps the trust and friendship they built in the first season. Thanks to that relationship and that foundation, there is a part of Matty that wants to stay and help Olympia, and doesn’t want her family to get hurt as a result of their investigation. Bates has this kind of internal struggle masterfully on display. In addition, Olympia has to balance Matty while protecting the father of her children. Leaving this storyline in the first season would have been a huge missed opportunity. In a genre known for playing it safe, Matlock took a risk, and it\'s paying off in every possible way. (Simone Risoluti/Vatican Media/\xadHandout via Reuters) Pope Leo XIV has told a group of leading Hollywood actors and filmmakers that more should be done to protect struggling neighbourhood cinemas in order to preserve the shared experience of watching movies. According to ABC News, screen stars Cate Blanchett, Monica Bellucci, Chris Pine and Oscar-winning director Spike Lee were among the celebrities to greet the pope at an audience in the Vatican on Saturday. Leo, the first pope to have been born in the United States, told the group the cinema industry was a vital "workshop of hope" at a time of global uncertainty and digital overload. Leo says cinemas are experiencing a troubling decline, with many being removed from cities and neighbourhoods. He is urging institutions not to give up, but to cooperate in affriming the social and cultural experience value of this activity. Box office revenues in many countries remain well below the levels recorded before the COVID-19 pandemic, with multiplexes in the United States and Canada just suffering their worst summer since 1981, excluding the COVID shutdown. Published Nov 15, 2025, 9:47 AM ET Updated Nov 15, 2025, 11:04 AM ET PUBLISHED Nov 15, 2025, 9:47 AM ET The US director Spike Lee gave Leo a basketball jersey at the meeting. Simone Risoluti/Vatican Media/Reuters Facebook Tweet Email Link Link Copied! Hollywood stars met Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican, where the pontiff called cinema a “workshop of hope” and lamented declining audiences. The line-up of film stars and directors meeting the first American pope on Saturday included Oscar-winners Cate Blanchett, known for “Aviator” and “Elizabeth”, and Spike Lee, who directed “Malcolm X” and “BlacKkKlansman”. All those present in the audience in the Vatican’s apostolic palace met Leo personally at the end, with Lee presenting the first American pope with a New York Knicks jersey. Monica Bellucci, who played Mary Magdalene in Mel Gibson’s “The Passion of the Christ”, also met the pope on Saturday, as did actor Adam Scott, of the series “Parks and Recreation” and “Severance”, and Sergio Castellitto, who played the “vaping cardinal” Tedesco in the movie “Conclave” that dramatizes the secretive papal election process. “The Church esteems you for your work with light and time, with faces and landscapes, with words and silence,” Leo told them. “I wish to renew this friendship because cinema is a workshop of hope, a place where people can once again find themselves and their purpose.” The meeting took place, the Vatican said, to “deepen dialogue with the World of Cinema” and explore the “possibilities that artistic creativity offers to the mission of the Church.” It also comes as the church is seeking to reach new audiences with a new Gallup World Poll showing a 17-point drop in the percentage of adults in the US who say religion is an important of their daily life. Pope Leo walks on the day of an audience with international filmmakers and actors, including Cate Blanchett, Spike Lee, Viggo Mortensen, Monica Bellucci, and Gus Van Sant. Simone Risoluti/Vatican Media/Reuters Cate Blanchett reacts in the Galleria Lapidaria of the Apostolic Palace after meeting Pope Leo. Matteo Minnella/Reuters In his speech, delivered in Italian, Leo also lamented the “troubling decline” of cinemas, which he said were increasingly being removed from cities. “I urge institutions not to give up, but to cooperate in affirming the social and cultural value of this activity,” he said in remarks that were greeted by an applause. The Chicago-born pontiff had shared his favorite movies ahead of the meeting, naming “It’s a Wonderful Life” (1946), “The Sound of Music” (1965), “Ordinary People” (1980), and “Life is Beautiful” (1997). Rev. Antonio Spadaro, one of the Vatican officials helping to arrange the meeting, reflected that in each of Leo’s chosen films “goodness appears fragile, naïve, almost out of place – and yet precisely for that reason, revolutionary.” The Vatican meeting with film stars follows a similar gathering hosted by Pope Francis with comedians. This event will take place at the Apostolic Palace on Saturday morning. Among the attendees are Academy Award-winning actors such as Cate Blanchett, Chris Pine, Viggo Mortensen, and Monica Bellucci, as well as directors like Spike Lee and George Miller. Pope Leo’s Engagement with Cinema This gathering highlights Pope Leo’s aspiration to engage with the film industry. The Vatican’s culture office is organizing the event as part of the ongoing Holy Year celebrations. A statement released by the Vatican emphasized the pope’s desire to enhance dialogue with the cinematic world. He aims to explore how artistic creativity can complement the Church’s mission and promote human values. Notable Attendees Cate Blanchett Chris Pine Viggo Mortensen Alison Brie Dave Franco Monica Bellucci Spike Lee George Miller Giuseppe Tornatore Gus Van Sant The Pope’s Favorite Films In a notable gesture of connection with filmmakers, Pope Leo recently shared his four favorite films: “It’s a Wonderful Life” (1946) by Frank Capra “The Sound of Music” (1965) by Robert Wise “Ordinary People” (1980) by Robert Redford “Life Is Beautiful” (1997) by Roberto Benigni Recent Interactions with Hollywood This event is unprecedented at the Vatican. Previously, the late Pope Francis hosted a gathering in June 2024 for comedians, including well-known late-night talk show hosts. Recently, Pope Leo met with actor Robert De Niro and his children, who were in Rome for a prestigious award ceremony and the opening of the Nobu Hotel Roma. Al Pacino also had an official audience with Pope Leo earlier this year, marking a significant moment for the first pope from the United States. As Pope Leo embarks on this Hollywood meeting, it underscores his commitment to bridging the gap between the Catholic Church and the film industry, inviting dialogue and cultural exchange. The celebrity meeting was a sprinkling of star dust for a still relatively new pope and a way for the Catholic Church to engage more with the world beyond. It was also a strong show of support from Leo XIV for the global film industry, as he spoke out against the "troubling decline" in cinema-going. Hailed by director Spike Lee as a "great day", the gathering was the first of its kind in the Vatican. Beneath the magnificent frescoes of the Clementine Hall, Pope Leo spoke in Italian to praise the power of cinema to entertain and to educate â\x80\x93 and for its "capacity to amaze". But he urged filmmakers not to shy away from what he called "the world\'s wounds". "Violence, poverty, exile, loneliness, addiction and forgotten wars are issues that need to be acknowledged and narrated," the Pope said. "Good cinema does not exploit pain; it recognizes and explores it. This is what all the great directors have done." Six months since a conclave of cardinals elected the first North American to the Papacy, some Catholics feel that Leo has been slow to stamp his own mark on the role. His predecessor, Francis, was a charismatic Argentinian known for his off-the-cuff comments and dramatic gestures. Leo\'s style is far quieter, so this star-studded engagement is a new look. It\'s not clear how the cast list was drawn up, although none of the directors in the hall â\x80\x93 who came from all over the world â\x80\x93 made it onto the Pope\'s own top film list. This week, the Vatican revealed that his favourite four watches of all time included the 1960s nun-themed classic The Sound of Music, It\'s a Wonderful Life and Italian Roberto Benigni\'s multi award-winning Life is Beautiful. Among those who did join today\'s A-list audience were Mortensen, Chris Pine and filmmaker Gus Van Sant â\x80\x93 of Milk and Good Will Hunting fame. The large Italian contingent included Gianni Amelio and Cinema Paradiso creator, Giuseppe Tornatore. At a time of immense pressure on film, not long after a major Hollywood strike and with funding strains here in Italy, the Pope spoke in defence of the industry. He was applauded loudly when he talked of the "quiet dedication" of all those behind the scenes with vital roles. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The audience for the international filmmakers was held beneath the magnificent frescoes of the Clementine Hall He also warned against the closure of cinemas which he characterised as the "beating heart of communities". "More than a few people are saying that the art of cinema and the cinematic experience are in danger. I urge institutions not to give up, but to cooperate in affirming the social and cultural value of this activity," the Pope said. After a fifteen-minute speech and a blessing he then received each audience member in turn, led by Blanchett . "He really urged us to go back into our day jobs and inspire people," the Australian-born star told reporters. One of many who came bearing gifts, the actress â\x80\x93 who works with the UN refugee agency, UNHCR â\x80\x93 placed a woven bracelet in the Pope\'s hand. "It was a bracelet I wear in solidarity with people who are displaced," she explained later. Lee handed the Chicago-born Pope a New York Knicks shirt printed with the number 14 and the words Pope Leo. The line-up of film stars and directors meeting the first American pope on Saturday included Oscar-winners Cate Blanchett, known for “Aviator” and “Elizabeth”, and Spike Lee, who directed “Malcolm X” and “BlacKkKlansman”. All those present in the audience in the Vatican’s apostolic palace met Leo personally at the end, with Lee presenting the first American pope with a New York Knicks jersey. Monica Bellucci, who played Mary Magdalene in Mel Gibson’s “The Passion of the Christ”, also met the pope on Saturday, as did actor Adam Scott, of the series “Parks and Recreation” and “Severance”, and Sergio Castellitto, who played the “vaping cardinal” Tedesco in the movie “Conclave” that dramatizes the secretive papal election process. “The Church esteems you for your work with light and time, with faces and landscapes, with words and silence,” Leo told them. “I wish to renew this friendship because cinema is a workshop of hope, a place where people can once again find themselves and their purpose.” The meeting took place, the Vatican said, to “deepen dialogue with the World of Cinema” and explore the “possibilities that artistic creativity offers to the mission of the Church.” It also comes as the church is seeking to reach new audiences with a new Gallup World Poll showing a 17-point drop in the percentage of adults in the US who say religion is an important of their daily life. In his speech, delivered in Italian, Leo also lamented the “troubling decline” of cinemas, which he said were increasingly being removed from cities. “I urge institutions not to give up, but to cooperate in affirming the social and cultural value of this activity,” he said in remarks that were greeted by an applause. The Chicago-born pontiff had shared his favorite movies ahead of the meeting, naming “It’s a Wonderful Life” (1946), “The Sound of Music” (1965), “Ordinary People” (1980), and “Life is Beautiful” (1997). Rev. Antonio Spadaro, one of the Vatican officials helping to arrange the meeting, reflected that in each of Leo’s chosen films “goodness appears fragile, naïve, almost out of place – and yet precisely for that reason, revolutionary.” The Vatican meeting with film stars follows a similar gathering hosted by Pope Francis with comedians. There are no “Evil Dead” titles. “The Exorcist” is suspiciously absent. The list, in this case, is the favorite four films of Pope Leo XIV, f.k.a. Robert Francis Prevost of Chicago. The pontiff released the list via video ahead of a planned meeting Saturday with luminaries from the world of cinema. To avoid the risk of being played off the stage by the academy’s orchestra, let’s share the winners quickly: Advertisement 1. “It’s a Wonderful Life,” 1946 2. “The Sound of Music,” 1965 3. “Ordinary People,” 1980 4. “Life Is Beautiful,” 1997 That’s it. No “The Agony and the Ecstasy.” No “Pope Joan” or “Spotlight” or “Conclave,” for obvious reasons. No “Sister Act” or “Oh, God!” or any of the associated sequels, for less obvious reasons. For the record: 11:28 a.m. Nov. 14, 2025 A previous version of this story said the pope hadn’t chosen any films set near his hometown, Chicago. “Ordinary People” was set in a Chicago suburb. As a matter of fact, not a single comedy at all, much less a goofy comedy. And on either the drama or comedy fronts, the pope definitely could have chosen more than one flick set in his former neck of the woods. Think “The Blues Brothers,” “Home Alone,” “The Untouchables,” “High Fidelity,” “Eight Men Out” or “Ferris Bueller’s Day Off.” (Think “Chicago ,” for goodness’ sake.) Pope Leo will apparently be meeting Saturday with Hollywood types including, Variety reports, actors Monica Bellucci, Cate Blanchett, Alison Brie, Dave Franco, Viggo Mortensen and Chris Pine, plus directors Spike Lee, George Miller, Giuseppe Tornatore and Gus Van Sant. Seems the pope “has expressed his desire to deepen dialogue with the World of Cinema, and in particular with actors and directors, exploring the possibilities that artistic creativity offers to the mission of the Church and the promotion of human values,” according to a statement obtained by CNN . Advertisement That sounds all well and good, and a person can’t really go wrong with the movies on the pope’s list — two of the four are best picture Oscar winners, and the other two are best picture nominees. That said, let’s shed a tiny tear for the exclusion of “Bruce Almighty,” if only because Morgan Freeman could use a little papal recognition too. Now, even more so, as he has revealed his all-time favorite films in a recent conversation with Variety. The Pope’s selection reflects an appreciation for works that have become both cultural landmarks and cinematic touchstones, films that, to borrow the words of Martin Scorsese, embody what “absolute cinema” can be. The first film mentioned by him is widely regarded as one of the best Christmas movies ever made, Frank Capra’s 1946 classic It’s a Wonderful Life. No wonder, in 1998, the American Film Institute named It’s a Wonderful Life the 11th greatest American movie of all time. Next on Pope Leo XIV’s list was a universally beloved musical, The Sound of Music (1965), starring Julie Andrews. It is hardly surprising that the film went on to win five Academy Awards, as it so thoroughly deserved to. The Pope also cited Ordinary People (1980), a family drama that explores grief and healing within a wealthy American household. The film is often hailed as a gold standard for cinematic portrayals of mental health and emotional vulnerability. Finally, the Pontiff named the Italian masterpiece La Vita è Bella (Life Is Beautiful), a moving World War II film that balances tragedy and humor in its portrayal of a father’s love for his son. After all, tragedy and comedy are often two faces of the same truth. Hollywood stars met Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican, where the pontiff called cinema a “workshop of hope” and lamented declining audiences. The line-up of film stars and directors meeting the first American pope on Saturday included Oscar-winners Cate Blanchett, known for “Aviator” and “Elizabeth”, and Spike Lee, who directed “Malcolm X” and “BlacKkKlansman”. All those present in the audience in the Vatican’s apostolic palace met Leo personally at the end, with Lee presenting the first American pope with a New York Knicks jersey. Monica Bellucci, who played Mary Magdalene in Mel Gibson’s “The Passion of the Christ”, also met the pope on Saturday, as did actor Adam Scott, of the series “Parks and Recreation” and “Severance”, and Sergio Castellitto, who played the “vaping cardinal” Tedesco in the movie “Conclave” that dramatizes the secretive papal election process. “The Church esteems you for your work with light and time, with faces and landscapes, with words and silence,” Leo told them. “I wish to renew this friendship because cinema is a workshop of hope, a place where people can once again find themselves and their purpose.” The meeting took place, the Vatican said, to “deepen dialogue with the World of Cinema” and explore the “possibilities that artistic creativity offers to the mission of the Church.” It also comes as the church is seeking to reach new audiences with a new Gallup World Poll showing a 17-point drop in the percentage of adults in the US who say religion is an important of their daily life. Pope Leo walks on the day of an audience with international filmmakers and actors, including Cate Blanchett, Spike Lee, Viggo Mortensen, Monica Bellucci, and Gus Van Sant. Simone Risoluti/Vatican Media/Reuters Cate Blanchett reacts in the Galleria Lapidaria of the Apostolic Palace after meeting Pope Leo. Matteo Minnella/Reuters In his speech, delivered in Italian, Leo also lamented the “troubling decline” of cinemas, which he said were increasingly being removed from cities. “I urge institutions not to give up, but to cooperate in affirming the social and cultural value of this activity,” he said in remarks that were greeted by an applause. The Chicago-born pontiff had shared his favorite movies ahead of the meeting, naming “It’s a Wonderful Life” (1946), “The Sound of Music” (1965), “Ordinary People” (1980), and “Life is Beautiful” (1997). "Good cinema does not exploit pain; it recognizes and explores it. This is what all the great directors have done." By: Entertainment Desk Mumbai | Updated: November 12, 2025 06:13 PM IST 3 min read Whatsapp twitter Facebook Reddit PRINT Pope Leo XIV Naturally, whatever Pope Leo XIV, the head of the Roman Catholic Church, says becomes a global talking point . Now, even more so, as he has revealed his all-time favorite films in a recent conversation with Variety. The Pope’s selection reflects an appreciation for works that have become both cultural landmarks and cinematic touchstones, films that, to borrow the words of Martin Scorsese, embody what “absolute cinema” can be. The first film mentioned by him is widely regarded as one of the best Christmas movies ever made, Frank Capra’s 1946 classic It’s a Wonderful Life. No wonder, in 1998, the American Film Institute named It’s a Wonderful Life the 11th greatest American movie of all time. Next on Pope Leo XIV’s list was a universally beloved musical, The Sound of Music (1965), starring Julie Andrews. It is hardly surprising that the film went on to win five Academy Awards, as it so thoroughly deserved to. The Pope also cited Ordinary People (1980), a family drama that explores grief and healing within a wealthy American household. The film is often hailed as a gold standard for cinematic portrayals of mental health and emotional vulnerability. Finally, the Pontiff named the Italian masterpiece La Vita è Bella (Life Is Beautiful), a moving World War II film that balances tragedy and humor in its portrayal of a father’s love for his son. After all, tragedy and comedy are often two faces of the same truth. Having written over 300 articles in just over a year, Billy regularly covers the biggest TV shows and films releasing while also analysing some of the most underrated properties that may slip your attention. Having studied for an MA in Screenwriting at UAL in 2023, Billy honed his writing skills and also developed his ability to critique the work of other creative minds. Before that, Billy studied politics at the University of Nottingham, which helped him to bring nuanced and scholarly analysis to the frameworks within which filmmakers and writers have framed their thematic messages. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap A24 is rightfully respected as one of the most artistic studios in Hollywood, going through a meteoric rise with films like Moonlight , Hereditary , and Everything, Everywhere, All at Once , putting it at the center of discussion in different genres and always around awards season. However, one of their best films has tragically gone under the radar: 20th Century Women . This coming-of-age drama features a stacked cast that examines how people find their purpose and true nature, and whether those are determined by the self or by society. The film was nominated for Best Original Screenplay at the Academy Awards, but that doesn\'t give nearly enough credit to the trio of actresses who carry the narrative and make it so engaging. Despite being set in 1979, the film\'s themes feel incredibly relevant to this day and, despite being incredibly indie, never feels overdone or like it is taking itself too seriously. It will make you laugh and cry, but as 20th Century Women argues, that is far better than feeling nothing at all. \'20th Century Women\' Explores a Mother and Son\'s Strained Relationship Annette Bening smoking a cigarette in 20th Century Women. Image via A24 Mike Mills \' exceptional drama centers on the relationship between Dorothea ( Annette Bening ) and her son, Jamie ( Lucas Jade Zumann ). Since he went through adolescence, Dorothea finds it increasingly difficult to connect with her 15-year-old son, as he seems not only not to know himself, but also to be a part of a generation increasingly more divisive compared to their predecessors, which fits with the counter-culture setting of the late 1970s. In an effort to reconnect and help her son discover who he wants to be, Dorothea enlists the help of her tenant, the punk-rock Abbie ( Greta Gerwig ), and Jamie\'s best friend, the depressed and opinionated Julie ( Elle Fanning ). However, that doesn\'t mean Dorothea doesn\'t have her own issues to contend with, as her generation is too closed off to truly speak their mind, which serves as the true source of conflict in her relationship with her son. There are tonnes of comedy and wild moments featuring funny sexual encounters and blunt lines of dialogue, but the tragic undertone running throughout 20th Century Women means the comedy feels like only a brief distraction from the engaging issues these characters are going through. Greta Gerwig, Annette Bening, and Elle Fanning Shine in \'20th Century Women\' As the title of the film and this article suggest, the stars of 20th Century Women are undoubtedly Bening’s Dorothea, Fanning’s Julie, and Gerwig’s Abbie, especially when they are in scenes together, because all three are so different. Each of them has a different idea of how to help Jamie become a man. Abbie believes he must learn about women to understand how to be a good man towards them, introducing him to feminist theory , whereas Julie has a more toxic idea of masculinity that she has developed through her experiences with boys of her age, believing what she sees must be the correct way of being. Dorothea arguably gives Jamie the most free rein to be who he wants to be, but more because of her own lack of self-analysis that she refuses to examine. Posts 2 By Daniela Gama Aug 13, 2025 In hindsight, Bening feels dreadfully snubbed with her lack of accolades for this performance. Her performance portrays her as both caring and emotionally stunted. When Jamie abandons her at one point to go to the city with some friends, she is clearly worried about him, telling him to let her know next time, yet she won\'t show that to anybody. She instead uses the excuse that she merely wants to know if she shouldn\'t cook as much dinner next time, a heartbreaking deflection that balances both her lack of honesty and her desire to provide for her son. \'20th Century Women\' Feels Remarkably Relevant to Today Throughout 20th Century Women , it is impossible to forget that it is set in 1979, with the wardrobe, constant smoking, and politics all reminding the viewer they are in the past. However, that doesn\'t stop it from feeling extremely pertinent to the challenges facing many people today. The idea of how men should interact with, not shy away from, feminism is a topic still fiercely debated online, yet no better moment encapsulates the contemporary relevance of 20th Century Women than when it shows Jimmy Carter\'s "Crisis of Confidence" speech. In this speech, the former President remarks on how everyone feels like they are lacking a purpose, that we all feel there is meant to be more to life than the current format. Indeed, with the rise of identity politics, people\'s individual sense of purpose has never been more unknown, yet Carter\'s argument, and seemingly Mike Mills\', is that the purpose is not that of the individual, but of society. In the same way that Jamie needs a range of different people to raise him, society needs a range of lived experiences living together cohesively to survive. Few will come away from 20th Century Women without learning something about themselves or those around them. Perhaps that is what makes it so underrated. It has such a key message that has been ignored for far too long. But you can change that. Do not go into 20th Century Women with preconceived notions about what kind of person you should be. Like Dorothea and Jamie, use it as an opportunity to see how you can connect with those around you, and your personal development will follow in time . 20th Century Women is available to stream for free on Tubi in the U.S. 20th Century Women Like Follow Followed R Drama Comedy Release Date December 28, 2016 Runtime 119 Minutes Director Mike Mills Writers Mike Mills Cast See All Annette Bening Dorothea Fields Elle Fanning Julie Hamlin Greta Gerwig Abbie Porter Billy Crudup William Where to watch Close WHERE TO WATCH Streaming RENT BUY Genres Drama , Comedy Powered by Expand Collapse Google is updating how content is shown. That’s where Catherine Bloom comes in. In her capacity as the longtime go-to personal shopper at Neiman Marcus, she became the style whisperer to the industry elite, her influence visible at most major red carpets. “Catherine Bloom is a staple name in Hollywood,” says stylist Linda Medvene, whose clients include Denzel Washington, Annette Bening and Geena Davis. “She always has pieces you can’t find anywhere else.” Related Stories News Welcome to Hollywood! Coffee Shop Says About You Given Bloom’s decades-long tenure at Neiman Marcus, it caused a stir in L.A. fashion circles this year when she took her talents to rival Nordstrom, which hired her as its first director of luxury styling. In late October, she opened her own store under the retailer’s auspices: Catherine Bloom for Nordstrom. “We want to invite you into our home,” Bloom tells THR about the expansive new studio. “It’s very warm, beautiful and chic, with a more interesting assortment than you’re traditionally used to seeing in most stores.” Interior designer Brigette Romanek, whose clients include Beyoncé and Gwyneth Paltrow, was hired to overhaul the space. “What made this project truly special was the synergy with Catherine,” says Romanek. “This wasn’t just about designing a space — it was about creating a mood, a moment, an experience.” Perched on the corner of Melrose Place and Orlando Avenue, complete with valet and a discreet side entrance, the by-appointment-only studio is drenched in neutrals: cream floors, a plush chocolate brown sofa, suede wall coverings and an array of vintage seating vignettes. And lining the walls are the stars of the show — meticulously curated racks of color-coordinated confections courtesy of such designers as Georges Hobeika, Gabriela Hearst and Valentino, along with McQueen and vintage John Galliano for Dior. Bloom’s industry clientele would expect nothing less. “Catherine is the ultimate curator,” says Blair Rich, CMO and CCO of Legendary Entertainment. “It’s more than just searching the Paris collections for the perfect dress and matching it with a shoe you never thought of but makes the look. She understands lifestyle; what you need not just to look your best but also feel your best, from the office to a black-tie event to a casual weekend away.” This story appeared in the Nov. 5 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Murphy directed and wrote the screenplay for Running with Scissors , which was released in 2006. The former Westworld cast member starred alongside an all-star cast that included Annette Bening, Alec Baldwin, Gwyneth Paltrow, Gabrielle Union and Kristin Chenoweth. Now Murphy and Wood are back together on a new project, a TV show called The Shards , which will air on FX, according to Deadline . Rounding out the cast are Kaia Gerber, Igby Rigney, Homer Gere, Graham Campbell and Hayes Warner. Wood's role hasn't been revealed yet, but she will star as a recurring character. The show is an adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis' 2023 novel The Shards , which takes place at a high school in the 1980s. The story focuses on a tragedy that occurs after a new student arrives. Ellis is best known for writing American Psycho , which was turned into a film starring Christian Bale. Running with Scissors , which was critically panned despite winning multiple awards, was released while Murphy's medical drama Nip/Tuck was on the air and three years before his hit musical comedy series Glee catapulted his career into the stratosphere. Since then, Murphy has created, produced and written numerous shows like American Horror Story , Scream Queens , American Crime Story , Feud , 9-1-1 and Pose . The multi-hyphenate creator has multiple shows currently on the air, including 9-1-1 and 9-1-1: Nashville . The Ed Gein Story , the third season of his Monster anthology series, was released on Netflix on October 3. It only has a 21% on Rotten Tomatoes, making it the lowest-rated installment of the true crime series. Murphy is about to launch a star-studded legal drama on Hulu called All's Fair with Sarah Paulson, Niecy Nash, Naomi Watts, Kim Kardashian, Teyana Taylor and Glenn Close. Aside from The Shards , he's got other shows in the works, including The Beauty and Love Story . Wood, meanwhile, followed up her role in Running with Scissors by starring in such films as The Ides of March , Across the Universe , Frozen 2 and Weird: The Al Yankovic Story , as well as the TV shows True Blood and Westworld , the latter of which earned her a Critics' Choice Award, a Golden Globe nomination and two Emmy nominations. Including Running with Scissors , Murphy's track record has certainly been mixed when it comes to the critical reception of his projects, so it's way too early to tell how The Shards will be received by the public. However, the novel it's being adapted from received mixed reviews but was a bestseller nonetheless. The movie with an all-star cast and some really funny aliens bombed at the box office, but it didn’t deserve to. In fact, I would say it’s one of Burton’s best movies . It had a reported budget of around $80 million, not including marketing, and it made about $100 million in theaters. That's not the worst performance, but it almost certainly lost a lot of money, something a Burton film rarely does. (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) At The Time, It Was Crushed By Critics In his 1996 review of the movie, Roger Ebert wrote : “ Mars Attacks! plays like one of those ’50s movies that are *not* remembered as cult classics.” Rita Kempley at the Washington Post said it was “aimlessly plotted and blandly written.” Review after review panned the tribute to ‘50s sci-fi movies. That was reflected, obviously, in the middling-to-poor box office receipts. Over the years, however, critics have come around. Burton, unsurprisingly, was ahead of his time. If the critics weren’t ready for it then, more modern critiques have been much kinder to the film, and it’s deserving of that. Very deserving. Mars Attacks! Is A Great Movie If you take yourself back to 1996, Burton was at the height of his powers in Hollywood. Starting with his first movie , Pee-Wee’s Big Adventure in 1985, he made one great film after another. A list including Beetlejuice , Batman, and Edward Scissorhands , the latter of which kicked off a long working relationship with Johnny Depp . It really seemed like the quirky director with a look and style all his own couldn’t be stopped. Then, in 1994, he hit his first bump in the road with Ed Wood . That film, a biopic of the legendary B-movie director, was a small-budget movie that generated modest box office receipts. Mars Attacks! followed in 1996 and was his first legitimate bomb. It shouldn’t be remembered for that (and isn’t). Burton enlisted a truly talented roster of actors for the movie that included up-and-comers like Natalie Portman and Lukas Haas. This was alongside some of Hollywood’s most established talent, like Michael J. Fox , Glenn Close, Danny DeVito , Sarah Jessica Parker , Annette Bening, Martin Short , and James Bond himself, Pierce Brosnan . It also crucially features Jack Nicholson in one of his most underrated performances in not one, but two roles. Mars Attacks! is also really funny and just plain fun. It’s completely absurd in all the best ways, and in ways that only a mind like Burton’s could imagine. I’m glad it is well thought of today, because otherwise, it would be another lost classic. (Photo by Jordan Strauss/Invision/AP) State officials will be unveiling a Florida Historical Marker in Fort Lauderdale on Thursday to commemorate Diana Nyad\'s incredible 110-mile swim from Cuba to Key West without a shark cage. Succeeding on her fifth attempt at age 64, Nyad became the first person to swim from Cuba to the Keys without a shark cage — despite battling stinging jellyfish, nausea and other physical and mental challenges. She completed the historic feat in 2013. Nyad\'s swim was later turned into a feature film , "Nyad," starring Annette Bening as the swimmer and Jodie Foster as Stoll, her friend and trainer. The recognition is particularly significant as Nyad is also the first openly LGBTQ+ person in Florida to receive a state historical marker. The dedication ceremony will be held at the Las Olas Oceanside Park in Fort Lauderdale. It is set to begin Thursday at 10 a.m. and is open to the public. Admission is free. The event is scheduled to feature remarks from local and state leaders, as well as members of the LGBTQ+ and women\'s communities and friends of Nyad. Speaking to Rolling Stone for the 30th anniversary of the film’s release, he said, “Look, [ The American President ] is a romantic comedy, but the two political issues at the heart of it were guns and the environment, right? The heroes I wrote in those two stories, they did things even though it would cost them popularity, which is not something you see professional politicians of either party do very often.” The feature, directed by Rob Reiner, follows popular Democratic president Andrew Shepherd (Michael Douglas) seeking reelection. But when the widowed incumbent falls for an environmental lobbyist (Annette Bening), a Republican challenger (Richard Dreyfuss) spots an opportunity to launch an attack campaign. Meanwhile, as Shepherd’s approval rating slips, he seeks to secure the passage of a crucial gun control bill. When asked if The West Wing creator sees any parallels between Republican officials and Dreyfuss’ Bob Rumson, he said, “All I see in the Republican Party today is a creepy, weird fealty to someone who doesn’t deserve it.” He continued later in the interview, “During Covid, I binged every Netflix documentary about cults — NXIVM and the Way Down Cult and Sarah Lawrence, everything. And what they all have in common is this weird, passionate devotion to an utterly unremarkable person. That’s where I feel we are now. I see the man-on-the-street interviews where people are calling Donald Trump authentic and honest, and he means what he says, [I think] you got to be kidding me. What’s new is this strange, cult-like devotion to the very last person who would deserve it. The electorate changed, and I’m not good at explaining what changed it. Maybe the left drove people out of their minds.” Sorkin has previously spoken about how his projects centering on civic duty would translate to modern audiences in our current political landscape. Last year, he voiced similar sentiments , saying of the right-wing party portrayed in The West Wing : “Right now, it would be implausible that the opposition party, that the Republican Party, was reasonable. People would watch that and it would be unfamiliar to them as the country they live in. On the show, while the Republicans were the opposition, they were reasonable.” The filmmaker/writer is currently working on the anticipated followup to 2010’s The Social Network , for which he penned the script. Titled The Social Reckoning , the drama is slated for release Oct. 9, 2026. Marvel Studios announced the first 27 actors cast in Avengers: Doomsday back in March, including members of the Avengers, New Avengers, Fantastic Four, X-Men, and more, all coming together to fight Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom. This caused some confusion, however, as some of the MCU’s biggest characters weren’t included in this announcement, but there has been speculation that many more will be involved. Videos by ComicBook.com This includes Carol Danvers’ Captain Marvel, who made her MCU debut back in Captain Marvel in 2019, and has since made appearances in Avengers: Endgame, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, Ms. Marvel, and The Marvels in 2023. A new image shared by Captain Marvel actor Brie Larson on her Instagram Story (via @MCUFilmNews ) urges viewers to “Ignore the wig!!” The wig in question is clearly lengthy and blonde, leading many to suspect that Larson will be reprising the role of Carol Danvers in Avengers: Doomsday , which is expected to be undergoing additional filming soon. Brie Larson in a newly shared photo! 👀 “Ignore the wig!! 🤫” pic.twitter.com/sfi8YKdcR5 — MCU Film News (@MCUFilmNews) November 5, 2025 What Role Could Captain Marvel Have In Avengers: Doomsday? Despite receiving a great deal of undue criticism from a vocal minority, Captain Marvel is one of the most important, powerful, and game-changing characters existing in the MCU right now. It would be a huge shame if she wasn’t involved with Avengers: Doomsday , especially since she not only has an intimate knowledge of the MCU’s cosmos — which will play a role in the Russo brothers’ upcoming sequel — but also because she is now residing on Earth. Danvers could easily be recruited into Sam Wilson’s new Avengers team , perhaps even becoming a leader among them. Read Next The MCU’s Biggest Box Office Bomb Still Deserves a Sequel Danvers’ most recent adventure in The Marvels directly contributed to the development of the Multiverse Saga, and this could be paid off in Avengers: Doomsday . After Dar-Benn (Zawe Ashton) collected both Quantum Bands, she accidentally tore a hole in the fabric of reality which Monica Rambeau (Teyonah Parris) managed to seal, but this trapped her on the other side. Rambeau was met by X-Men members Beast (Kelsey Grammer) and Binary (Lashana Lynch), perfectly setting up the appearance of the X-Men in Avengers: Doomsday , but only if Rambeau returns — and her Aunt Carol shouldn’t be far behind. Captain Marvel’s almost-unmatched level of power, given to her after she absorbed the energy of the Space Stone from Mar-Vell’s (Annette Bening) light-speed engine, means Danvers may be powerful enough to go toe-to-toe with Doctor Doom. Doom is expected to scour the multiverse in Avengers: Doomsday in hopes of stopping incursions by destroying other worlds and variants, but he’ll come under opposition by many of the MCU’s heroes. Danvers held her own against Thanos (Josh Brolin) in Endgame , so would also be an invaluable asset in the fight against Doom in Doomsday , so we really hope she returns. What do you think? Bassyonni 26 Nov 2025 Home News Sports Entertainment Tech Business Home Entertainment Aaron Sorkin: Studios Unlikely to Produce ‘The American President’ Today Entertainment Aaron Sorkin: Studios Unlikely to Produce ‘The American President’ Today Bassyonni ago 9 days Oscar-winning screenwriter Aaron Sorkin recently expressed skepticism about the current film industry’s willingness to produce a movie like his 1995 classic, The American President. In an interview with Rolling Stone, he reflected on the film’s themes, noting that studios today might hesitate due to its political messaging. Aaron Sorkin on The American President’s Modern Relevance Sorkin argued that the film’s dual focus on guns and environmental issues could alienate potential viewers. He pointed out, “A studio wouldn’t agree to make it because they would know you’ve just alienated half the potential audience.” This sentiment highlights the changing landscape of political discourse and audience reception since the film’s release. Overview of The American President Director: Rob Reiner Release Year: 1995 Stars: Michael Douglas as President Andrew Shepherd, Annette Bening as an environmental lobbyist, Richard Dreyfuss as Republican challenger Bob Rumson The plot centers on President Shepherd as he navigates reelection while facing both political and personal challenges. As his approval ratings drop, he tries to push through a significant gun control bill amid a budding romance with a lobbyist. Sorkin’s Views on Today’s Politics Sorkin also drew parallels between contemporary political figures and Rumson’s character, expressing concern over a “cult-like devotion” to unremarkable leaders. He linked this phenomenon to a broader shift in the electorate, stating, “The electorate changed, and I’m not good at explaining what changed it.” Reflecting on his previous work, Sorkin mentioned that the portrayal of the Republican Party in The West Wing would seem unrealistic to modern viewers. He stated, “Right now, it would be implausible that the opposition party was reasonable.” Such comments underscore the evolving perception of political dynamics among audiences. Upcoming Projects Currently, Sorkin is working on his new project, The Social Reckoning, which serves as a sequel to his acclaimed film, The Social Network. It is expected to premiere on October 9, 2026. As Sorkin continues to explore themes of civic duty and political engagement, the challenges of adapting to today’s audience remain evident. His insights into The American President emphasize the complexities of modern storytelling in a politically charged environment. Having written over 300 articles in just over a year, Billy regularly covers the biggest TV shows and films releasing while also analysing some of the most underrated properties that may slip your attention. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap A24 is rightfully respected as one of the most artistic studios in Hollywood, going through a meteoric rise with films like Moonlight , Hereditary , and Everything, Everywhere, All at Once , putting it at the center of discussion in different genres and always around awards season. However, one of their best films has tragically gone under the radar: 20th Century Women . This coming-of-age drama features a stacked cast that examines how people find their purpose and true nature, and whether those are determined by the self or by society. The film was nominated for Best Original Screenplay at the Academy Awards, but that doesn\'t give nearly enough credit to the trio of actresses who carry the narrative and make it so engaging. Despite being set in 1979, the film\'s themes feel incredibly relevant to this day and, despite being incredibly indie, never feels overdone or like it is taking itself too seriously. It will make you laugh and cry, but as 20th Century Women argues, that is far better than feeling nothing at all. \'20th Century Women\' Explores a Mother and Son\'s Strained Relationship Annette Bening smoking a cigarette in 20th Century Women. Image via A24 Mike Mills \' exceptional drama centers on the relationship between Dorothea ( Annette Bening ) and her son, Jamie ( Lucas Jade Zumann ). Since he went through adolescence, Dorothea finds it increasingly difficult to connect with her 15-year-old son, as he seems not only not to know himself, but also to be a part of a generation increasingly more divisive compared to their predecessors, which fits with the counter-culture setting of the late 1970s. In an effort to reconnect and help her son discover who he wants to be, Dorothea enlists the help of her tenant, the punk-rock Abbie ( Greta Gerwig ), and Jamie\'s best friend, the depressed and opinionated Julie ( Elle Fanning ). However, that doesn\'t mean Dorothea doesn\'t have her own issues to contend with, as her generation is too closed off to truly speak their mind, which serves as the true source of conflict in her relationship with her son. There are tonnes of comedy and wild moments featuring funny sexual encounters and blunt lines of dialogue, but the tragic undertone running throughout 20th Century Women means the comedy feels like only a brief distraction from the engaging issues these characters are going through. Greta Gerwig, Annette Bening, and Elle Fanning Shine in \'20th Century Women\' As the title of the film and this article suggest, the stars of 20th Century Women are undoubtedly Bening’s Dorothea, Fanning’s Julie, and Gerwig’s Abbie, especially when they are in scenes together, because all three are so different. Each of them has a different idea of how to help Jamie become a man. Abbie believes he must learn about women to understand how to be a good man towards them, introducing him to feminist theory , whereas Julie has a more toxic idea of masculinity that she has developed through her experiences with boys of her age, believing what she sees must be the correct way of being. Dorothea arguably gives Jamie the most free rein to be who he wants to be, but more because of her own lack of self-analysis that she refuses to examine.
